titleReview.originalTitle: View the health of your disaster recovery plans in NetApp Disaster Recovery
titleReview.titleReasoning: The current title is long and uses a conversational construction. A shorter task title that starts with a strong verb and omits the product name fits NetApp title conventions better because the product context is already supplied by site navigation.

fileInfo.userGoal: View the health and status of disaster recovery sites and replication plans

leadReview.originalText: Using the NetApp Disaster Recovery Dashboard, you can determine the health of your disaster recovery sites and replication plans. You can easily assess which sites and plans are healthy, disconnected, or degraded. You can also review recent warnings and failed jobs, see which workloads are protected and are not, and see an overview of capacity.
leadReview.suggestedRevision: Use the NetApp Disaster Recovery Dashboard to check the health of your disaster recovery sites and replication plans. You can see whether sites and plans are healthy, disconnected, or degraded, review recent warnings and failed jobs, identify protected and unprotected workloads, and view capacity at a glance.
leadReview.leadReasoning: The revision removes filler phrasing, improves parallel structure, and makes the user value clearer and more concise.

titleReview.originalTitle: Create a replication plan in NetApp Disaster Recovery
titleReview.titleReasoning: The title follows a task pattern, but it unnecessarily includes the product name and can be shortened. A concise imperative title better matches NetApp standards.

fileInfo.userGoal: Create a replication plan to protect resources and define failover mappings

leadReview.originalText:
After you've added resources and sites, create a _replication plan_ to manage data protection. Creating the replication plan involves designating the source and destination sites, selecting the resource groups, and choosing how applications should be restored and powered on. For example, you might group virtual machines (VMs) associated with one application or you might group applications that have similar tiers.

When you create a replication plan, you can also edit schedules for compliance and testing, performing test failovers without impacting your production data.
leadReview.suggestedRevision: After you add resources and sites, create a _replication plan_ to protect your data. The plan defines the source and destination sites, resource groups, recovery mappings, and power-on behavior for your applications. You can also configure compliance and test schedules and perform test failovers without affecting production data.
leadReview.leadReasoning: The revision reduces repetition, removes the example that slows the opening, and focuses the lead on what the page helps the user accomplish.

fileInfo.userGoal: Create a resource group for protected resources

leadReview.originalText: After you've added resources to sites, you can create resource groups to organize VMs, datastores, or Kubernetes clusters as a single unit. Resource groups enable you to organize a set of dependent resources into logical groups that meet your requirements. For example, you might group VMs associated with one application or you might group applications that have similar tiers. As another example, groups could contain delayed boot orders that can be run upon recovery.
leadReview.suggestedRevision: After you add resources to sites, create resource groups to organize VMs, datastores, or Kubernetes clusters as a single unit. Resource groups let you organize dependent resources into logical groups that meet your requirements. For example, you can group VMs for one application or group applications that share similar tiers. Resource groups can also include delayed boot orders that run during recovery.
